### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (36 routes)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `afe83b254b6d62ff3a39e7eda3148383146ffeb4` — the merge of head `7fb21edeac2cd17e8c047e1cc0f8bc6366cc63ca` into base `ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin afe83b254b6d62ff3a39e7eda3148383146ffeb4 && git checkout afe83b254b6d62ff3a39e7eda3148383146ffeb4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55 7fb21edeac2cd17e8c047e1cc0f8bc6366cc63ca && git checkout -B drift-repro ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55 && git merge --no-ff 7fb21edeac2cd17e8c047e1cc0f8bc6366cc63ca

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ab3c776a957f18f3f61c0fc85dec7180b31bca55` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf3ec26820915712eb0a7aea1de8a1ce7a89134a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts + packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json, packages/spec/export-origins/ai.json, packages/spec/src/ai/mcp-oauth-scopes.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts (registerToolFromDefinition, registerAuthoringTools, bridgeTools, handleHttpRequest), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (grantsAuthoringTools beside registerObjectTools / registerActionTools / wireBridgeTools), packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, packages/mcp/src/types.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.authoring-scope.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md.authoring.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts (handleMcpRequest, handleMcpSkillRequest), packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts (oauthScopes), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts (verifyMcpAccessToken), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts (oauthProvider scopes roster), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (scopes_supported), packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts (ToolExecutionContext), ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/OAuthConsentPage.tsx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (PROTOCOL_BASELINE_ROOTS), docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json, .changeset/26464-mcp-metadata-write-scope.md, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx, packages/mcp/README.md

Read as a p1 security review, adversarially: the question on every path was whether an authoring tool can be listed or called without a verified `metadata:write` grant, and whether anything a client sends can reach a tool's provenance. Card #26464 carries four comments at read time (filing, triage, the server-seat re-lane, the claim); no os-dev report comment exists yet, so there are no `out_of_scope` / `open_questions` to answer.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Fail-closed — holds on every path read.**
- The only gate is `grantsAuthoringTools(grantedScopes)` = `Array.isArray(grantedScopes) && grantedScopes.includes('metadata:write')` (mcp-http-tools.ts), read once in `registerAuthoringTools` before any `registry.getAll()`; without it the function returns `[]` and the registry object is never touched (pinned: `registry.calls` stays empty on data:write, actions:execute, empty and undefined grants).
- `grantedScopes` reaches the runtime from one place: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` reads `ec.oauthScopes`, which `assemble-execution-context.ts:384` sets ONLY for a verified OAuth token (`oauth && authz.userId === oauth.userId ? oauth.scopes : undefined`). An API key or a session cookie therefore arrives as `undefined`, which the authoring predicate refuses (deliberately stricter than the native families' "undefined = not scope-limited"). The dispatcher adds no `authoring` injection at all, so the OSS runtime serves nothing authoring on any path; the injection exists only for a host (cloud#3302).
- Scope spelling: `verifyMcpAccessToken` splits the JWT `scope` claim on a single space and keeps the strings verbatim (no lowercasing, no trimming of other whitespace); every downstream read is an exact `includes`. So `Metadata:Write`, a tab-joined claim, a trailing-space variant, `metadata:*` or `*` all fail closed — and a token carrying none of the four exact strings is refused 403 up front by the dispatcher's `some(includes)`. A token minted before the scope existed simply lacks the string.
- `undefined` vs `[]`: both refuse authoring; for the native families `[]` also registers nothing (pinned: tools/list on an empty grant answers an error because no `tools` capability is declared).
- Registration is per request: `handleHttpRequest` builds a fresh `McpServer` per POST, calls `registry.getAll()` on that server and closes it in `finally`; the injection is a call parameter, nothing is cached on the shared `MCPServerRuntime` instance, and the stdio `this.mcpServer` is never touched by the HTTP path. No cross-request leak is possible from this code.

**(b) Refusal parity — holds, with no existence leak.** An unregistered authoring tool gets exactly what `create_record` gets without `data:write`: the SDK's unknown-tool answer from the same `McpServer`, no second dialect. The pin reads either SDK shape (JSON-RPC error on older SDKs, `result.isError` on the pinned 1.32.1 — the package range is `^1.30.1`) and asserts the authoring text equals the native text once the tool name is swapped. `tools/list` with a registry injected and no scope is pinned byte-equal to `tools/list` with no registry, so a client cannot learn an authoring tool exists from either the list or the refusal.

**(c) Provenance — built from host inputs alone; no header or argument reaches it.** `registerAuthoringTools(server, authoring, grantedScopes, logger)` has no `Request` in scope; the per-call context is `{ door: MCP_TOOL_DOOR, actor: { id: principal.userId }, principal, environmentId? }` with `door` a module constant and the other two the host's call arguments. Tool arguments travel as `toolCall.input` in the FIRST parameter; the context is the SECOND, so no argument key can shadow `door` / `principal` / `environmentId`. The seven spoofed headers (`x-door`, `x-objectstack-door`, `x-environment-id`, `x-user-id`, `x-forwarded-user`, `x-organization-id`, `x-principal`) are pinned as absent from the serialised context. `opts.authInfo` is forwarded to the transport only and is not read by the bridge. A fresh context object is built per call (pinned across two calls with a tainting handler).

**(d) stdio and the native tools — byte-identical.** The registration body moved from a private method to the module function `registerToolFromDefinition` with one `execute` seam; I compared the removed and added bodies hunk by hunk (registration options, `toolCallId` spelling, the `isError` and `catch` envelopes, `formatToolOutput`) — identical. `bridgeTools` passes a closure that calls `toolRegistry.execute(call)` with one argument, pinned through a real stdio session (`arities = [1]`). `wireBridgeTools`, `registerObjectTools`, `registerActionTools` are untouched in the diff (mcp-http-tools.ts gains only an import and the new predicate; it imports nothing from `./`, so `skill-md.ts` importing it creates no cycle). `handleMcpSkillRequest` still renders with `{ mcpUrl }` only, so the OSS skill route never renders the authoring section.

**(e) Semver and the declaration lines — correct.** The diff moves `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json` and `export-origins/ai.json` (two added consts) and NO `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard (verified against the merge base). `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades the level on the METADATA PROTOCOL alone: `PROTOCOL_BASELINE_ROOTS` is exactly those two authorable directories; `api-surface/` is not a protocol baseline, it is the `check:api-surface` export ratchet. `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES` feeds no Zod schema in `packages/spec/src` (grep: zero non-test readers), so nothing an author writes gained a value. Hence `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, `patch` on both packages is what `none` requires (a `minor` would be refused as `none-minor`), and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right for added exports, an added scope value and an optional new parameter. The `Check Changeset` run on this head concluded `success`, agreeing with that reading.

**(f) The requestable scope list — deliberately widened, and safe.** `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES` is read by the AS: `oauthProvider({ scopes: [openid, profile, email, offline_access, ...MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES] })` (the roster DCR clients may request) and `scopes_supported: [...MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES, 'offline_access']` (discovery), plus the dispatcher's 403 prose and `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. So a client can now request `metadata:write` and a user can consent to it on every deployment, which the PR body names as intended ("the first readers that come for free"). Safe because a token carrying it gains nothing but the authoring family a host injects: `scopesToAgentPermissionSets` maps it to the no-object-access floor and changes no data ceiling beside a data scope (pinned), `delegatesActions` still keys on `actions:execute` alone, and on the OSS runtime (no injection) a `metadata:write`-only token reaches `handleHttpRequest`, registers zero native tools and is served no tool capability. The gaps that remain are consent-copy and advertising gaps, listed under ③, not grants.

**Tests pinned as read:** 17 cases in `mcp-server-runtime.authoring-scope.test.ts` cover the gate on four grant shapes, parity, provenance, seven spoofed headers, fresh context, absent environment, isError / throw paths and stdio arity; `skill-md.authoring.test.ts` pins every other render byte-identical; `skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts` pins the rendered skill against the registered surface with and without the scope; `mcp-oauth-scopes.test.ts` pins the four-scope order, one sentence per scope and the data-ceiling invariance.

**Check-runs on this head** (read 2026-10-27T07:51:29Z; 47 runs): 25 `success`, 7 `skipped` (opt-in harnesses, dogfood, Temporal Conformance, `Lint UI`, `Test UI` — path-scheduled, no `ui/` in the diff), 15 `in_progress`. Of the eight required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Lint UI` skipped; `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` and the four `Type Check ·` lanes still in progress. `Check Changeset` success. No run has concluded `failure`. The verdict below is on the diff; the in-progress gates are the landing's own condition ("every check is green"), not this record's.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/mcp`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset — correct per ① (e). Nothing is removed or narrowed: no tombstone, no ADR-0087 marker, no migration owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

None blocking. For the record and for the consumers named:

1. **OSS consent screen shows the raw string (dev-flagged, UI lane).** `OAuthConsentPage.tsx` maps the three agent scopes in a `switch` and renders anything else as its spelling, so an OSS user asked for `metadata:write` consents to "metadata:write" with no sentence. The PR's `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_CONSENT_COPY` is NOT yet read by the Console (it uses i18n keys `oauth.consent.scope.*`). The scope is advertised everywhere from this PR on, so a `ui/` card wiring the page to the constant (or adding the i18n key) is owed — Prime Directive #10 names a user-facing consent with no description as a trap worth its own card, not an acceptance note. Not blocking: the consent is still an explicit grant, and the scope grants nothing on OSS.
2. **OSS advertises a scope no OSS reader serves anything under.** `scopes_supported` and the challenge now name `metadata:write` on a deployment whose dispatcher passes no `authoring`; a token holding it is admitted and served no tool. Fail-closed, so not a grant, but it is a scope-with-nothing-behind-it on the open runtime until a host injects (Route & surface ownership rule 4 tension). Acceptable here because the card orders the scope in spec with its first reader in `@objectstack/mcp`, and `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES` is single-sourced by design; worth one line in the OSS docs if the OSS dispatcher never gains an injector.
3. **Host contract for cloud#3302 — three things the runtime cannot check for the host:** (i) the gate reads `toolOptions.grantedScopes`, not `authoring.principal.scopes`; the host must derive both from the same verified token or the context will carry scopes the gate did not read. (ii) `principal` is stamped by reference, not copied or frozen; an injected tool that mutates `context.principal.userId` in place taints the host's object for the next call (and the next request, if the host reuses it). The fresh-context pin covers replacement, not in-place mutation. Tools are host-trusted code, so this is hardening, not a hole — `principal: { ...principal }` or `Object.freeze` would close it in one line. (iii) `McpServer.registerTool` throws on a duplicate name, and `registerAuthoringTools` runs after `wireBridgeTools`; a host injecting a tool named like a native one (`create_record`, `run_action`, …) turns the request into the dispatcher's 500, never a shadowed native tool. The host must keep its names disjoint.
4. **Skill prose vs a `metadata:write`-only grant.** The authoring section renders for any grant naming `metadata:write` and tells the model "Discover first here too — `describe_object`", which is a `data:read` tool and is not registered for a token without that scope. The surface-guard pin holds the other direction (every registered tool is named); this direction (a named tool not registered) is a model-facing nuisance, not a boundary. One conditional sentence fixes it.
5. **Stale prose, no gate.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json` clause `ai.mcp-http-surface` says the 403 names "all three scopes"; the challenge now lists four. The dev notes it for the QA sweep; anchors are intact.
6. **Pre-existing, out of this diff:** `assemble-execution-context.ts:384` turns an OAuth principal whose `userId` differs from the resolved `authz.userId` into `oauthScopes: undefined`, i.e. "not scope-limited" for the native families. Unchanged by this PR and irrelevant to authoring (undefined refuses it), noted only because a reader of (a) will meet it.
